prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 6 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same moment's world, painted together: the same people, props, weather, light and colour grade in every panel.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Food three-wheeler. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; office worker is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): One image contains six equal portrait panels arranged three across and two down, read left to right, with narrow plain gutters. Identity and performance are conveyed through pose only, without human features or clothing. It is early morning in Colombo, with soft daylight entering from frame right, open pavement shade, restrained warm colour and slightly desaturated, film-like contrast. The older maroon three-wheeler has a black vinyl roof, raised serving hatch, scratched stainless-steel ledge, dark-brown trim and worn silver fittings. The working flask is dull stainless steel with shallow dents, a dark-brown handle, screw lid and narrow spout. Shallow trays contain golden triangular pastries, oval rolls and round cutlets; a small aluminium kettle and folded cleaning cloth occupy the cramped ledge. The customer's plain cup contains caramel-brown milk tea only after service. All surfaces and objects are painted realistically. No lettering, numerals, captions, symbols or readable vehicle plates appear anywhere.

Geography: The story moves from the roadside approach to the food counter a few steps farther along the same pavement. The three-wheeler is parked beside the near kerb, with its cab toward frame left and its open serving compartment extending toward frame centre. Low shops and a mustard scalloped awning stand behind it. Across the road, a flat-roofed bus shelter with two dark posts provides the connecting landmark: it remains on frame right in the street view and every counter view. At the counter, the camera stays on the public side, looking obliquely along the ledge so Kasun occupies frame left and the customer space opens toward the road on frame right. The office worker faces left toward Kasun; his eventual departure is toward screen right. The closer profile view remains on this same side of their axis.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing eye height on the near pavement, looking along the two receding traffic lanes; vertical wide shot with a 28mm feel and deep focus. Background: Parked tuk-tuks and the mustard shop awning line frame left. Low shopfronts, blank signboards and the two-post bus shelter occupy frame right; the road recedes through the centre. A bus, a tuk-tuk and a motorcycle occupy the roadway, with only the maroon cab and black roof of the food three-wheeler cropped into the extreme left edge; its serving opening is outside the image. A small grey rider sits on the motorcycle facing into the receding lane, chest and head aligned with the handlebars and both hands gripping them. Two distant grey pedestrian mannequins stand apart on the far pavement, one beside the shelter and one beside a shopfront, both with chests and heads facing screen left and hands lowered. Reflections conceal the occupants of the enclosed vehicles.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing eye height on the public side near the cab end, looking obliquely along the serving ledge; torso-up medium shot with a 50mm feel. Background: The maroon compartment and shadowed shelving sit behind Kasun on frame left. The raised hatch borders the top; the road and recognisable bus shelter remain softly visible on frame right. The red mannequin stands behind the ledge at frame left, chest facing screen right toward the work surface and head angled down toward the pastries. Its right hand grips the upright flask above the ledge, while its left hand hovers just over the nearest row of short eats. The trays fill the lower right, with the kettle and folded cloth fitted into the narrow remaining counter space.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Standing eye height on the same public side, with a slightly wider view along the ledge; waist-up two-shot with a 35mm feel, including the customer's lowered cup. Background: Maroon bodywork and the hatch interior remain behind Kasun on frame left. The open customer side, road and distant two-post bus shelter occupy frame right. The red mannequin stands at frame left with chest and head turned screen right toward the blue mannequin, its right hand holding the flask upright at chest height over the ledge and its left hand resting near the trays. The blue mannequin stands at the far right edge, a half-step back from the counter, with chest and head facing screen left toward Kasun. Its right hand holds an empty cup down beside its hip at the lower-right edge, while its left hand hangs freely at its side.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height at the earlier public-side working position, looking obliquely along the ledge; medium shot with a 50mm feel. Background: The maroon compartment fills the left background. A narrow strip beyond the blue mannequin reveals the road and the same bus shelter at far frame right. The red mannequin remains behind the ledge at frame left, chest and head facing screen right toward the customer, with its right hand holding the flask upright above the counter and its left hand beside the trays. The blue mannequin still stands in the right third, slightly inward from the edge, with chest and head facing screen left. Its right hand holds the filled cup near the ledge, a faint wisp rising above the tea, and its left hand rests at its side.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Standing eye height, closer on the same public side and aligned for a clean right-facing profile; medium close-up with an 85mm feel and shallow focus. Background: A narrow maroon hatch edge remains at frame left. Soft roadway shapes fill frame right, including the blurred horizontal roof and dark posts of the same bus shelter. The red mannequin's head and upper torso fill the left half in a clean right-facing profile, with chest and head aligned toward the road at screen right. The crop excludes both hands and the flask. Open road blur occupies the right half, leaving clear space in the direction the head points.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Standing eye height at the same public-side position as the earlier working medium shots; torso-up medium shot with a 50mm feel, including the low-held flask. Background: Maroon bodywork and shadowed shelves remain on frame left. The road and softly resolved two-post bus shelter stay on frame right beyond the empty customer space. The red mannequin stands at frame left with chest and head still turned toward the road at screen right, rather than down toward the food. Its right hand holds the upright flask low beside its torso at the lower edge of the panel, while its left hand hangs relaxed beside the nearest tray without touching the pastries. The short eats occupy the mid-right ledge, with the kettle and folded cloth unchanged beside them.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.
